title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
read_level: full (arXiv HTML v1; main text Secs 1-8, Tables 1-7; appendices B/C only skimmed; figures as text only)
metadata_mismatch: none in title/authors; minor wording differences between metadata abstract and HTML abstract (e.g. metadata 'using 158 agent turns' / 'own BF16 weights' vs HTML 'utilizing 158 agent turns' / 'native BF16 weights')
why_wsp: Replaces the LLM agent of Takehi et al.'s Qwen3.5-0.8B loop repair with a forward-statistics objective solved as per-row QUBO/Ising problems (simulated annealing or simulated bifurcation) that pick sparse sign flips and power-of-two exponent shifts in stored BF16 weights.
facets: application domain: LLM math reasoning (reasoning loops)
domain: LLM math reasoning; repairing thinking-mode reasoning loops
editor: none (solver): simulated annealing / simulated bifurcation on GPU; 8-variable QAOA proof of concept on IBM Heron
target: Qwen3.5-0.8B down_proj of layers 15 and 19 (1,024 x 3,584 each); transfer to Qwen3.5-2B (down_proj 2,048 x 6,144, layers 15 and 19)
loop: one-shot (fixed recipe: 4 forward-pass requests incl. one validation screen)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "Tree-Ising modifies 13% fewer weights (affecting only 1.5% of the two matrices)" (Sec 4.4); Table 5: agent edit 130,188 changed weights vs Tree-Ising (SA) 112,630, (SB) 108,327. Qwen3.5-2B: "the patch modifies a mere 1.2% of the weights across the two matrices" (Sec 5).

headline_results.claim: MATH-500 vs agent edit, same harness
headline_results.quote: Tree-Ising achieves 54.6% on MATH-500, outperforming the agent's edit (51.7%) under an identical evaluation protocol, while the base model scores only 7.9%
achieving 55.1% on MATH-500 with 4% fewer modified weights
MATH-500@4 +2.9 ± 1.0 points, z=2.94 , p≈0.003 (better on 108 problems, worse on 73)
On the remaining 400 problems ... Tree-Ising achieves 53.8% accuracy compared to 50.8% for the agent edit

headline_results.quote: the discrepancy with the originally reported 48.1% appears to stem from the initial evaluation setup rather than our harness
Applying the unchanged recipe elevates GSM8K accuracy from 21.6% to 69.4%
this continuous solution scores 57.8% on the screen ... However, it fundamentally alters 96% of the weights across both matrices
the depth-two QAOA circuit sampled the optimum in 110 out of 1,024 shots, compared to merely four shots for a uniform control

baselines_and_controls: GPT-6 Astra agent edit of Takehi et al. (re-evaluated in same harness); base model; ablations of beta, move set, budget, dose, greedy solver; continuous closed-form rank-one (ROME-like) edit rounded to BF16; plain directional ablation (38.3% on screen); QAOA vs uniform sampling.
runs_and_variance: Single generation seed per benchmark; paired per-problem tests with Bonferroni over 12 comparisons. Quote: 'Each benchmark evaluation utilized a single generation seed.' and 'Each solver was executed only once with a single seed' (Sec 8).
robustness_of_edits: not tested (no fine-tuning/quantization survival tests; instruction following and non-math benchmarks not evaluated)
verification: none formal; exact enumeration verifies optimum for the 8-variable QAOA instance only
memorization_vs_reasoning: n/a (no LLM editor); recipe was designed retrospectively from the agent's public logs and reuses its layers/dose on 0.8B
limitations_stated: Single failure mode, one model family, math benchmarks only; base 7.9% not rerun; development leakage on 100 MATH-500 problems; recipe derived from agent logs, not dose-matched; layer exclusion rule set after inspecting scan; first-order surrogate objective; single seeds; QAOA shows no quantum advantage.
code_or_data: https://github.com/TheQuantumGOAT/Tree-Ising (stated 'will be made publicly available shortly'); agent logs cited at https://github.com/RikiyaT/lm_understand-logs
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 MIT CSAIL weight-space programming blog/logs (refs [54],[55])
independent reproduction of agent checkpoint, ref [32] (51.0% MATH-500)
notes_for_survey: Yes, it reports the 89.7M tokens and 15.6 hours figures for the original GPT-6 Astra edit, derived from the released 50-pass logs (Table 4). Cost comparison contrasts the agent's discovery run with applying a recipe built afterwards from its logs, which the authors state explicitly. The 2B transfer removes dependence on the agent's layer and dose choices.
